title: 投资经典：企业购并案例 — Day 29
title_en: Investing Classics: Acquisition Case Studies — Day 29

questions.question: Buffett 说「用公道价买伟大公司，远胜于用便宜价买平庸公司」。下面哪种做法其实误用了这条原则？
options: 认定某公司伟大，于是不管估值多高都买入
买入护城河清晰、能长期高回报再投资的公司，价格合理即可
买入前检查当前价格隐含的未来增长假设是否现实
对一家便宜但价值不增长的公司保持警惕，担心折价永不收敛
questions.explanation: 「公道价」不是「任何价」：1999 年许多人以「伟大公司」之名为科技股付出了永远收不回的价格，伟大公司买贵了也要十年才能填平。警惕便宜的平庸公司、检查隐含增长假设，都是这条原则的正确用法。
questions.question_en: Buffett said it's far better to buy a wonderful company at a fair price than a fair company at a wonderful price. Which of the following actually misuses this principle?
options_en: Buying a company at any valuation because you've decided it is wonderful
Buying a firm with a clear moat that can reinvest at high returns, as long as the price is reasonable
Checking whether the growth assumptions implied by today's price are realistic before buying
Being wary of a cheap company whose value doesn't grow, in case the discount never closes
questions.explanation_en: A fair price is not any price: in 1999 many paid unrecoverable prices for tech stocks in the name of 'great companies', and even a great company bought too dear can take a decade to catch up. Avoiding cheap mediocre firms and checking implied growth are correct applications.

questions.question: 一家股价暴跌的公司看起来很便宜。按 GEICO 1976 年的困境反转思路，决定能否买入的关键问题是什么？
options: 核心盈利机制受损了，还是只是财务或管理出了问题
市场情绪是否已经悲观到了极点
它的股价相对几年前的历史高点，是否已经跌得足够深
它过去是否曾是行业里的知名龙头
questions.explanation: 困境反转的核心是诊断而不是抄底：GEICO 直销的低成本护城河没坏，坏的是准备金和扩张，换了管理层就可修。Kodak、Sears 也曾是知名龙头、跌得很惨，但主业经济性本身在崩塌，接了就是飞刀。
questions.question_en: A company's stock has collapsed and looks cheap. Following Buffett's 1976 GEICO turnaround logic, what is the key question in deciding whether to buy?
options_en: Whether its core earning mechanism is damaged, or only its balance sheet and management
Whether market sentiment has reached maximum pessimism
Whether the price has fallen far enough from its historical peak
Whether it was once a well-known industry leader
questions.explanation_en: A turnaround bet rests on diagnosis, not bottom-fishing: GEICO's low-cost direct-selling moat was intact, while its reserves and overexpansion were fixable with new management. Kodak and Sears were also famous names that fell hard, but their core economics were collapsing — catching falling knives.

questions.question: Buffett 称 Dexter 鞋业是他做过最糟的交易。除了护城河被进口鞋摧毁，让这笔错误格外昂贵的原因是什么？
options: 他在亏损后不断追加资金，试图挽救这家公司
他用自家股票而非现金支付，送出的股权此后持续复利
他借了大量债务完成收购，利息拖垮了 Berkshire
他没做尽职调查、只凭一次握手成交，结果买到了财务造假的公司
questions.explanation: 约 4.33 亿美元的 Berkshire 股票到 2014 年值约 57 亿美元：现金支付的错误是有限的，股票支付的错误是复利的。「握手成交、不做审计」说的是 Nebraska Furniture Mart，那笔恰恰是成功案例。
questions.question_en: Buffett called Dexter Shoe his worst deal. Besides imports destroying its moat, what made this mistake so especially costly?
options_en: He kept pouring more money in after losses, trying to rescue the company
He paid in his own company's stock rather than cash, and the shares he gave away kept compounding
He financed the deal with heavy debt, and the interest dragged down Berkshire
He skipped due diligence and closed on a handshake, buying a company with fraudulent books
questions.explanation_en: About $433 million in Berkshire stock was worth roughly $5.7 billion by 2014: a cash mistake is bounded, a stock-paid mistake compounds. The handshake deal without an audit was Nebraska Furniture Mart — a success story.
